title: Is the kern_small / kern_big / kern_mega / kern_emu matrix and the near-model rule still the right shape, and what do they cost?

strengths.title: One product name per build, additive variants, nonsense combinations refused
strengths.why: Each build has exactly one product name. KERN_EMU and KERN_MEGA imply KERN_BIG, so no '%ifdef KERN_BIG' site misses them. small+emu, small+mega and emu+mega are %errors.

strengths.title: A feature-symbol configuration layer resolved above every include
strengths.why: About 700 conditionals test named features (OS88_DRIVERS, OS88_COMPACT, OS88_REDIR, OS88_IMG, FCP_MOD...) instead of a build name. Each is resolved once with its reason, which plays the role of SysV's master file in a tree with no linker.

strengths.title: Protected-mode cleanliness enforced by the assembler
strengths.why: KDS, KSEG, VSEG, CSDO and the rest are byte-identical to the real-mode instruction off kern_mega. Each is an %error in a section where its premise is false. About 400 sites (KSEG 54, CSDO 176, KDS 37, VSEG 22) serve both modes with no separate code path.

strengths.title: The XT does not pay for the 286, and that is proved
strengths.why: kern_big and kern_small are recorded byte-identical across every kern_mega-only change.

strengths.title: Budgets derived per kernel and all four checked at release
strengths.why: KERN_BUDGET, MEGA_RESIDENT and KERN_CODE_MAX are each derived from the kernel's own sections, and kernsize --release runs on the two extra kernels beside the shipped two.

strengths.title: Packages are one binary across kern_big and kern_small
strengths.why: The SDK keeps MAX_TASKS at 14 and MAX_WIN at 12 while kern_small runs 5 and 6, so a small kernel's snapshot is over-allocated rather than overrun. Windows' lesson that everything above the kernel is mode-portable is already learned for packages.

strengths.title: Separate code at build time and shedding at run time are both used where each fits
strengths.why: kern_small carries FCP_MOD and FDLG_MOD as on-demand modules, and kern_big drops its .vga rung at boot on mono machines.

findings.title: A fix made on one kernel's code path leaves the shipped kernel with the defect
findings.detail: osapi_drv_classk_x counts loaded rows only under %ifdef KERN_MEGA. kern_big keeps 'cmp ax,1' on the KB sum, yet kern_big's own HMA placement zeroes DRVR_PARA on a loaded row, so a loaded class reads as absent (drivers-3). HBM_BADV routes to .badv only on kern_mega, although .badv is assembled on kern_big inside OS88_IMG (hiber-2). The rule that kern_big must stay byte-identical across kern_mega work is the right proof for kern_mega's own mechanism. Applied to a cause in shared code, it leaves kern_big broken. Neither defect is in MEGA-RELEASE-PLAN 4.2's list of kern_big defects.
evidence: kernel/driver.inc:3933 and word [bx+DRVR_PARA], 0 ; no heap held
docs/plans/KERN-MEGA-PLAN.md:798 'kern_big assembles byte-identical with all of it'
findings.recommendation: Make both fixes unconditional. Add to KERN-MEGA-PLAN's checklist: a fix under %ifdef KERN_MEGA says why its cause is not in shared code; if it is, the fix lands unconditionally in the same commit. Rewrite CLASSK's header (doc mismatch D8).
findings.listed_as: drivers-3, hiber-2 (this review); not in MEGA-RELEASE-PLAN 4.2
findings.verify_note: drivers-3 confirmed: osapi_drv_classk_x counts rows only under %ifdef KERN_MEGA (driver.inc:2170-2209), and %1_hma (driver.inc:3933, under HMA_DRV, which kernel.asm:1176-1183 defines on kern_big/kern_emu with ROM_COLD and not on kern_mega) zeroes DRVR_PARA. hiber-2 confirmed, but the evidence is wrong: .badv is NOT assembled on kern_big inside OS88_IMG. The %ifdef OS88_IMG at hiber.inc:3404 wraps only .bimg; .b9/.b8/.b8s/.b7/.badv/.nox all sit inside the %ifdef KERN_MEGA opened at .b6 (3424-3466). Making the fix unconditional therefore means assembling .badv (and its hb_xseg free and hbm_vbk call) on kern_big too, not only re-pointing HBM_BADV. Bytes: the row-count arm is push/xor/inc/pop cx plus cmp cx,1 in place of cmp ax,1 = +5, not +6; HIBER.DRV grows by .badv's ~20 bytes on kern_big (module bytes, 0 resident). Neither item is in ABI-BREAK-LIST, KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE or MEGA-RELEASE-PLAN.

findings.title: kern_small's separate code fails at refusal stubs and guards, and no gate decodes them
findings.detail: Three of the four kern_small-only bugs are a stub or guard written apart from the full body. abi-2: OSAPI_XREFUSE clobbers AX on a cell whose contract says every register is kept. dw-8: the WRITE_AT stub enters below its neighbours' mov ax, FERR_NAME. video-1: the dual-card refusal is %ifdef KERN_BIG because vid_dual_ok lives there, although kern_small's vid_avail can hold both a CGA and a Hercules. t_api_abi reads build/kernel.bin only, and its FIXED ledger has no kern_small rows (abi-3).
evidence: kernel/kernel.asm OSAPI_XREFUSE macro and the FS_OP cell (abi-2)
findings.recommendation: Take abi-3's --kernel mode over smallk, emuk and megak with per-kernel FIXED rows. Give OSAPI_XREFUSE an argument naming the cell's refusal shape (KEEP = stc/retf, or AX=FERR_x), so a stub cannot be written without naming the contract it answers. Make the video-1 guard test the hardware capability it protects.
findings.bytes_est: 0 (gate); 0 abi-2 (cell stays 6 bytes); +0..+3 dw-8 and ~+6 video-1 on kern_small
findings.verify_note: abi-2, abi-3 and dw-8 confirmed by their own verifiers; video-1 corrected there (+13 kern_small, not ~+6). The guard is at fsx.inc:1034-1042 as cited, under %ifdef KERN_BIG. OSAPI_XREFUSE (kernel.asm:2595-2600) takes no argument and is used on four cells (0x04B3, 0x04CB, 0x04EF, 0x04F5), two of whose contracts differ, so a shape argument is a real guard. t_api_abi.py:457 opens build/kernel.bin only. Byte estimate for video-1 should read +13 (video.json).

findings.title: Test coverage per kernel is inverse to the product's floor
findings.detail:
From suite.rows() (2,034 rows):
- kern_big: about 1,490 soak rows and 12 full rows.
- kern_mega: about 430 soak rows (343 mega- ports). test-full never boots it.
- kern_small: 28 soak rows and one full row (small128).
- kern_emu: 1 row.

_ports already runs rows on kern_small's own build for 86Box (box86port.txt with @OS88_BUILD=build/smallk). There is no MartyPC lane, because _ports drops the 'marty' need and forces Bochs or 86Box. So the 128KB XT has no ported coverage on the instrument that models it.
findings.recommendation: Add tests/smallport.txt and a 'small-' prefix to _ports that keeps the base row's marty need. Seed it with rows covering the modules where kern_small has two diverging bodies: desk, diskw, disk, memory, files, wm, fsx, and the module seam (FCP/FDLG).
findings.verify_note: Counts are about right: a re-count over suite.rows() (2,034 rows) gives roughly 21-28 kern_small soak rows depending on how a row is attributed, ~390-430 kern_mega, and test-full's 14 rows contain no kern_mega boot (megahigh is a host check). tests/megaport.txt is 443 lines. Correction: no box86port.txt line runs on kern_small today - the grammar supports `@OS88_BUILD=build/smallk @OS88_DEFINES=KERN_SMALL` (box86port.txt:6-7, a comment), but none of its 45 lines uses it. _ports drops the marty need (suite.py:21775-21777) as stated, so a smallport.txt lane needs a parser change, not only a list.

findings.title: The parity gate covers kern_big and kern_small but not kern_mega, the only kernel whose every machine has a 16-bit bus
findings.detail: The parity gate (t_hotpar) pins HOT['big'] and, when the build is current, HOT['small']. It gives a reason for leaving kern_emu ungated and says nothing about kern_mega, although its own premise is that a word fetch at an odd address costs a second bus cycle on the 8086, V30 and 286. kern_small's 128KB machines are nearly all 8088s, where parity is free, yet it carries 9 build-gated hand pads; kern_mega carries 2. Each pad is tuned to one kernel, and a byte cut in shared code ahead of it flips parity on the kernels it was not tuned for.
evidence: pads: diskw.inc:193, font.inc:1010/1014/2069/2515, memory.inc:761, vga12.inc:4559, viddet.inc:1106, vidsel.inc:1634 (small); dock.inc:435, kernel.asm:6412, sched.inc:2770, wm.inc:7908 (big); instance.inc:723, mouse.inc:2260 (mega)
findings.recommendation: Pin HOT['mega'] in t_hotpar when build/megak is current. Replace the 15 build-gated pads with one HOTPAR even|odd macro: %if (($-$$)&1) != want / db 0 / %endif, placed at the same never-executed points. Section bases are even on every kernel, so the absolute form is sound.
findings.bytes_est: 0 net (0 or 1 byte per site per kernel, chosen by the assembler)
findings.verify_note: t_hotpar.py's main() checks HOT['big'] and HOT['small'] only and its docstring excuses kern_emu, not kern_mega. The self-aligning precedent exists in the tree (vidext.inc:103 and font.inc:620 use `%if ($ - label) & 1 / db 0 / %endif`), so the macro shape assembles. Pad line numbers have drifted a few lines (e.g. diskw.inc:197, memory.inc:773, instance.inc:727, mouse.inc:2267), which does not change the finding.

findings.title: Do not merge the kernels into one binary that picks its mode at boot (priced)
findings.detail:
Section sizes:
- kern_big: .text 40,328, .bss 5,366, .cold 37,566; KERN_SIZE 96,768 of 100,864.
- kern_small: .text 30,035, .bss 2,936, .cold 21,031; 58,880 of 64,000.
- kern_mega: .text 46,076, .bss 5,404, .cold 46,509, .mega 23,568; MEGA_RESIDENT 62,976 of 68,096.

kern_small as kern_big that sheds at boot needs tables sized for the large machine: task stacks 2,816 against 960 (+1,856) and the FAT window 4,608 against 1,024 (+3,584). That is +5,440 against 5,120 of headroom, before any run-time door. The VGA slide alone needs 14 registered doors, and the 64KB would stop being proved by the assembler.

kern_mega folded into kern_big is the section delta (.text +5,748, .cold +8,943) less .vga (2,030) and the KHP knobs (~452): about 12-14.7KB on every XT, against 4,096 of headroom. Windows 3.0 shipped KERNEL.EXE, KRNL286 and KRNL386 as separate binaries for this reason; 3.1 dropped the real-mode one.
evidence: build/smallk/kernel.map, build/megak/kernel.map section lengths; bytes.md M5 for kern_big
findings.recommendation: Keep four build-time kernels. Record this table in docs/KERNEL-MEMORY.md as the reason, so the merge is not proposed again as an obvious simplification.
findings.verify_note: Section sizes re-read from build/smallk/kernel.map (.text 0x7553 = 30,035, .bss 0xB78 = 2,936, .cold 0x5227 = 21,031) and build/megak/kernel.map (.text 46,076, .bss 5,404, .cold 46,509, .mega 23,568); kern_big .text 40,328, .cold 37,566, .vga 2,030 and KERN_SIZE 96,768 of 100,864 from kernsize. sched.inc:177 states 960 against 2,816; DSK_FAT_SECS is 2 (kernel.asm:1519) and 9 (:1565). +1,856 + 3,584 = +5,440 against 64,000 - 58,880 = 5,120. tests/vgarefs.txt has 14 registered doors. The mega deltas (.text +5,748, .cold +8,943) check.

findings.title: Retire kern_emu: rebuild VMMOUSE.DRV the way USBMOUSE.DRV works
findings.detail: kern_emu exists to carry VMMOUSE's resident half: a gate byte, vmm_dsp, vmm_poll from ui_task and task_yield, and mou_apply_abs, 385 bytes in all. It also changes the idle loop (sched.inc:764, 1810, 2370, 2503). kern_big already ships a polled pointer driver with no kernel poll site: USBMOUSE.DRV's worker yields rather than sleeps for UM_HOTT ticks after a report, and delivers through OSAPI_MOUSE_FEED. mou_apply is a plain add and clamp with no acceleration, so an absolute report converts exactly into a feed: dx = scaled_x - mouse_x, read via OSAPI_MOUSE. The 386 probe moves into the driver behind OSAPI_CPU_INFO.
evidence: SPEC.md 9.11.3 (vmm_poll in task_yield), 9.11.7 (385 bytes; 'kern_big plus this feature and nothing else')
findings.recommendation: Rebuild VMMOUSE.DRV as a DRVC_POINT worker driver on kern_big. Remove KERN_EMU: 21 blocks, make emu, build/emuk, emu.img, its kernsize --release leg, its _SHIPPED_DEFS entry and its buildmatrix leg. The browser live image boots kern_big with VMMOUSE.DRV ticked. Try one prototype against the vmmouse row before removing any kernel code.
findings.bytes_est: +~40 kern_big resident (drv_tab row, name, label, CFG bit); -385 kern_emu-only resident; one kernel build retired
findings.verify_note: A rethink, not a defect; spot-checked, and confirmed as a priced option rather than a proven design. SPEC.md 9.11.5/9.11.7 give the 385 bytes and 'kern_big plus this feature and nothing else'. USBMOUSE.DRV is a worker driver with no kernel poll site that feeds OSAPI_MOUSE_FEED and yields for UM_HOTT ticks after a report (usbmouse.asm:12-15, 88-90). mou_apply (mouse.inc:4151) is an add then mou_clamp with no acceleration, so an absolute-to-delta conversion is exact as long as the driver reads mouse_x/y at the time of the feed. Unproven: that a worker rotation pumps a drag's spin loop as promptly as vmm_poll inside task_yield (9.11.3's freeze argument), and the +~40 byte figure, which is an estimate - DRV_MAX rises 6 -> 7 on kern_big with a row's .bss. The recommendation's 'prototype first' covers both.

findings.title: Build names, not features, are still the main configuration language inside modules
findings.detail:
Census of conditionals naming a build:
- KERN_BIG: 636 blocks, 147 with two bodies (1,857 lines).
- KERN_SMALL: 124 blocks, 46 with two bodies (341 lines).
- KERN_MEGA: 406 blocks, 152 with two bodies (832 lines).
- KERN_EMU: 21 blocks, 3 with two bodies.

There are about 700 feature-symbol tests beside these. 'kern_small is kern_big minus named features' holds only where a symbol exists. A guard placed under a raw build name is how video-1 happened.
evidence: census script over kernel/*.inc and kernel.asm
KERN_BIG concentrations: ctrl.inc 95, wm.inc 85, vga12.inc 53, driver.inc 35
KERN_MEGA in shared files: memory.inc 58, hiber.inc 41, disk.inc 40, diskw.inc 30
findings.recommendation: Add a ratchet shaped like tests/textsites.txt. Build names may appear in kernel.asm's define block and in mega*.inc; every other site is registered with a reason, and a new one fails make. Sites move to named capability symbols as their files are touched. No bulk conversion.
findings.verify_note: Re-counted %if/%ifdef/%elif lines naming each build over kernel/*.inc and kernel.asm: KERN_BIG 638, KERN_SMALL 126, KERN_MEGA 406, KERN_EMU 21; per-file KERN_BIG ctrl.inc 95, wm.inc 82, vga12.inc 51, driver.inc 33 - within a few of the reviewer's census.

findings.title: Flattening kern_small to one code segment: priced, and not recommended while its ROM is a product
findings.detail: kern_small's .text + .bss + .cold is 54,002, which fits in 64KB. The crossings between .text and .cold cost about 540 bytes (bytes-4). On this kernel .cold buys only the ROM: there is no VGA rung to slide over and no HMA, and ROM_PKG puts a package in that ROM on kern_small alone. The crossings are written as literals (380 'call COLD_SEG:', 335 'call KERNEL_SEG:', plus §2.6.1's retf-ending entry bodies), so a flat build needs every one behind a macro first.
findings.recommendation: Refuse while kern_small's ROM is a product: 21,031 bytes of .cold plus a package off a 128KB heap outweigh 540. If the owner drops the ROM for kern_small, the trade reverses.
findings.verify_note: 380 `call COLD_SEG:` and 335 `call KERNEL_SEG:` re-counted. kernel.asm:1150-1153 says kern_small drives no VGA and has no rung to slide; ROM_PKG is kern_small-only at 1186-1191. 30,035 + 2,936 + 21,031 = 54,002. bytes-4 (-540) is confirmed in bytes.json.

findings.title: One disk set for the 8088 and the 286 (WIN.COM's half), after L3
findings.detail: kern_mega ships on its own 286-PLUS disks. Windows 3.0 chose the kernel in WIN.COM from one install, because NE ordinal linking made USER, GDI and the drivers portable across modes. os8088's kernel modules are bound to one kernel's layout (MOD_STAMP), so each kernel needs its own module set. A dual-kernel system disk would carry kern_mega's KERNEL.SYS (115,872 bytes) and its 11 modules (56,607), about 172KB: feasible at 1.2MB and 1.44MB only. Stage 2 reads the kernel as the first file in the data area, so a second kernel also needs a fixed placement in os88disk.py and a CPU and extended-memory test in .boot2. Packages still differ until L3.
findings.recommendation: Record as the product step that L3 enables, in this order: L3 plus megacore rethink 4's clean bit; then one apps disk; then the selector. Do not build the selector before L3.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: MOD_STAMP is a function of the kernel's section sizes (mod.inc:138-140), kernel.sys is 115,872 bytes and build/megak holds 11 .drv files totalling 56,607; mkzip.py:312-325 makes the 286-PLUS disks a separate required group.

findings.title: Budget headroom decides which kernel gets a speed-up
findings.detail: kern_mega carries KHP knobs 1-11 because 'its conventional budget had room'. Knobs 2-11 speed up desktop paths the XT runs slowest, for example KHP_RELIT (a CGA full-screen exit, 781 -> 629 ms) and KHP_RAISEOL (a CGA raise, -5 to -14 ms). Those ten cost about 452 bytes on kern_big, 214 of them in .vga, which is resident only on VGA/EGA machines. They ship only on the 286/386 kernel. This is the rung rule applied across kernels: one kernel's headroom is not a reason for another kernel to lack a feature.
findings.recommendation: Decide each knob by the target-machine question already used elsewhere: N bytes on kern_big for M cycles on the XT. For each one refused, record why kern_big says no.
findings.bytes_est: 0 now; +452 kern_big if all ten are taken (+238 .text/.cold, +214 .vga)
findings.listed_as: LAST-DROP-PERF 7.2/7.3; wm.md and sysmisc.md KHP findings
findings.verify_note: The weakness stands (kernel.asm:255-261: kern_mega carries the first eleven because 'its conventional budget had room'), and the bytes check: rows 2-11 of LAST-DROP-PERF 7.1 sum to 452, of which .vga is 122+39+21+32 = 214. But the recommendation is already largely done: LAST-DROP-PERF 7.1 prices each knob in kern_big bytes and XT time and has a 'why it is not on yet / what would flip it' column for every row, ranked for kern_big. What is left is the owner's per-row decision, not a new record.

findings.title: The near model still limits kern_big, at the VGA rung, with 6,946 bytes left
findings.detail: The VGA rung is reached by near calls, so its last byte must be a KERNEL_SEG offset. On kern_big it sits above .text, .bss, the FAT window and .lowbss, and kernel.asm calls its guard 'the binding form of KERN_CODE_MAX now'. kernsize reports 6,946 bytes left in that window. CLAUDE.md and KERNEL-MEMORY.md still define KERN_CODE_MAX as .text + .bss, which reads as 19,842 left. kern_mega (14,056 free) and kern_small (32,565 free) are not limited by it.
findings.recommendation: On kern_big, quote the window figure rather than KERN_CODE_MAX's; see doc mismatch D7. Note that a .lowbss or FAT-window byte on kern_big now costs window headroom as well as budget.
findings.listed_as: bytes-4 (figure quoted, not named as the binding one)
findings.verify_note: kernsize today: 'segment .text+.bss 45,694 of KERN_CODE_MAX 65,536 -> 19,842 left' and 'window the VGA rung ends at KERNEL_SEG:0xe4de -> 6,946 of the 64KB window left'. The guard is kernel.asm:8731 with the comment 'the binding form of KERN_CODE_MAX now'. kern_small 65,536 - 32,971 = 32,565. docs/KERNEL-MEMORY.md 1121-1124 and SPEC.md 4028-4029 already say this; only CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md's short form did not (doc fix applied).
